Topic: The Magic of Pure Fourier Series: Breaking Down Waves

Target audience: University students (Engineering/Physics/Mathematics)

Section: section_1 — Intuitive Hook: The Symphony of Waves

Lecture lines:
Complex waves hide simple building blocks.
A meow is just many sines.
Watch these waves add up perfectly.
Separate the waves into simple parts.
Reconstructing the signal is our goal.

Planned animations:
Create a wave visual on screen using #3498DB.
Pulse the wave with #E74C3C to draw attention.
Add a label 'Frequency Component' in #ECF0F1.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Refresher: Orthogonality

Lecture lines:
Periodic signals repeat over time.
Orthogonal waves behave like independent axes.
They do not interfere with each other.

Planned animations:
Show two perpendicular vectors with #2ECC71.
Dot product highlight in #F1C40F.
Fade in 'Orthogonal' text in #ECF0F1.

Section: section_3 — The Core Formula: The Fourier Recipe

Lecture lines:
The Fourier series is a mathematical recipe.
We sum sine and cosine components.
Weights determine the contribution of each.
Ingredients create a complex target shape.
Mixing waves builds the final function.

Planned animations:
Display f(t) = a0/2 + sum(an cos + bn sin).
Flash summation symbol in #E67E22.
Highlight 'a0' and 'an' terms in #3498DB.
Show component signals merging into one #9B59B6.
Group terms clearly for final formula review.

Section: section_4 — Calculating the Coefficients

Lecture lines:
Integrals extract our specific frequency coefficients.
The filter isolates one harmonic wave.
See the amplitude emerge from integration.

Planned animations:
Display integral formula for 'an' in #2ECC71.
Highlight dt differential in #F1C40F.
Fade in coefficients calculation step in #ECF0F1.
Show result shrinking as n increases in #E74C3C.
Update total signal sum on screen.

Section: section_5 — Application: The Digital Signal Processor

Lecture lines:
Fourier series power modern digital compression.
Adjusting coefficients filters audio noise away.
Equalizers show these principles in action.

Planned animations:
Show digital waveform samples as dots in #3498DB.
Overlay Fourier result curve in #E74C3C.
Highlight reconstruction error with small arrows.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Complex waves hide simple building blocks.", "A meow is just many sines.", "Watch these waves add up perfectly.", "Separate the waves into simple parts.", "Reconstructing the signal is our goal."]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Symphony of Waves", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3*x) + 0.3 * np.sin(5*x), color="#3498DB")
        label = Text("Frequency Component", font_size=20, color="#ECF0F1")

        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3498DB")
        self.place_in_area(wave, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#E74C3C")
        self.play(wave.animate.set_color("#E74C3C"), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ECF0F1")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'E3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#2ECC71")
        self.play(wave.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.5), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Application: The Digital Signal Processor", [

        ])

        for i, p in enumerate(points):
            p.move_to(np.array([-2.5 + i * 0.3, 0.5 * np.sin(i * 0.5), 0]))
            
        # Fourier curve

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3498DB")
        self.play(Create(points))
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#E74C3C")
        self.place_in_area(fourier_curve, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(fourier_curve))
        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#F1C40F")
        error_arrows = VGroup(*[
            Arrow(start=points[i].get_center(), end=fourier_curve.point_from_proportion(i/19), color=WHITE, buff=0.1, tip_length=0.1)
            for i in range(0, 20, 2)
        ])
        self.play(Create(error_arrows))
        self.wait(2)
